transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Over the last month I’ve just lost interest in my art, dancing, and even my job, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to. I just feel so flat, and I don't know how to get back to myself.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have you had similar episodes in the past?

This current low, flat feeling has been going on steadily for about five months now, starting not long after an intense tax rush at my job. Looking back, I've noticed these swings where I go from feeling overly revved up to sinking into these heavy, exhausted lows happening off and on for about five months.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you had much more energy than usual, lasting for several days or more?

Yes, right before this crash, I had about two weeks during the tax rush where I felt almost buzzed and super upbeat all the time. I had an unusual amount of energy, felt like I was on top of everything, and got a bit snappy or irritable if anyone tried to slow me down.
How many times have you had these episodes of high energy and mood, and how long did each one typically last?

These swings between feeling overly revved up and then crashing have been happening off and on for about five months now. The high-energy phases usually last for a couple of weeks at a time. During those weeks, I feel totally buzzed, super active, and barely need any sleep.
Have you had at least two distinct periods of elevated mood and increased energy, each lasting several days or more, in your lifetime?

Yes, I've had at least two of those distinct high-energy periods over the last five months. They usually last for a couple of weeks at a time, like the really intense one during tax season, before I inevitably crash back down.

These manic episodes, alternating with depressive symptoms over the past five months, support a diagnosis of bipolar disorder (F31) rather than unipolar recurrent depression (F33). The current presentation includes both manic and depressive phases occurring in a cyclical pattern, which is characteristic of bipolar affective disorder.
